hypothesis: Wave D20 (C_L3_SURVIVAL_BURN, L0): a closed living store lowers its burn as it shrinks, dR/dt = -P0 (R/R0)^beta, with beta calibrated on one fast (Benedict 1915, subject L.) at 1.95 (1.5-2.6 with the window). Expectation tested: an independent and far longer fast follows the same law with beta in that range; constant leak (beta = 1, D14) and constant burn (beta = 0) are excluded.

observable.quantity: beta_obs, the exponent from a least-squares fit of the D20 closed form (R0, P0, beta free) to body weight against time
observable.domain: one obese man during a supervised 382-day fast with non-caloric supplements, Stewart and Fleming (1973) Postgrad Med J 49, 203 (PMC2495396)

prediction_method.description: Weight points read after approval off the paper's body-weight figure (or a table, if the paper has one), as published; points from day 6 on; least-squares fit of the closed form R(t) = [R0^(1-beta) + (beta - 1) P0 R0^(-beta) t]^(1/(1-beta)). The fit was checked on synthetic fasts (beta 0, 1, 2 recovered within 0.03). The script refuses to run unless this card is APPROVED and the data sha256 matches.

fixed_parameters: beta range 1.5-2.6 from the Benedict calibration (R_D20_SURVIVAL_BURN), fixed before this fast is read
FAILED bounds beta < 1.2 or beta > 3.3 (AI choices; 1.2 keeps D14's beta = 1 inside FAILED)
pass_criterion: PASS if 1.5 <= beta_obs <= 2.6: the second fast slows its burn like the first.
fail_criterion: FAILED if beta_obs < 1.2 (no survival process beyond a constant leak) or beta_obs > 3.3. INCONCLUSIVE otherwise or with fewer than 6 points.
note: Disclosure: the drafter has not seen this paper's figure or text beyond its abstract metadata; from general knowledge it recalls only that the man went from about 207 kg to about 82 kg over 382 days, not the shape of the curve. The paper is a scanned 1973 article; the drafter believes its Figure 1 is the weight chart but has not looked; if no weight series exists the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE. beta was calibrated on a lean man over 31 days and is applied to an obese man over 382 days: a real out-of-sample test, and a hard one, since body composition differs. Supplements (vitamins, potassium, sodium, early yeast) were non-caloric. The power-law burn is an AI choice for the author's survival process. Nearest theory: metabolic adaptation in starvation (Keys 1950; Hall 2008). Not UET-distinct. Approved by the author in chat on 2026-11-25 as drafted ("Approve and run"); this approval is committed before the paper's figure or text is read.
